newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher in dull trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed up across the board on Tuesday in dull trading after the Jewish Passover holiday, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.09 pct to 105.63
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.13 to 104.56

"Nothing special happened today. People are still on holiday. The market has already digested the March consumer price index (CPI) and the fact that the central bank did not lower its interest rates," said a trader at IBI Investment House.

The Bank of Israel announced last Thursday that it was leaving unchanged its key lending rate for May. Its base rate has remained at an annualised 13.9 percent since the end of February. The March CPI rose by an unexpected 1.0 percent against forecasts of 0.7-0.8 percent.
"Trading in dollar-linked bonds was up, but not as much as the rise in the dollar, which indicates that traders don't expect the dollar to go up considerably," the trader said.
The Israeli shekel weakened against the dollar on Tuesday and the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4100 shekels to the dollar.

"The market rose because after four days of holiday yields have risen. All in all the atmosphere in the market is good because the coming CPIs, after that of April, are expected to be low," said Gila Shkury, investment adviser at Israel Discount Bank.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
